Every link below was loaded with `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200) and its page title checked, unless
noted. Official sources come first.

## Curated links

- **[NOT-OD-21-013: Final NIH Policy for Data Management and Sharing](https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-21-013.html)**
  (NIH Guide) — the policy itself. Use it to read Sections II, III, V, VII and VIII in full and to
  check any quote in the lesson. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Data Management & Sharing Policy Overview](https://sharing.nih.gov/data-management-and-sharing-policy/about-data-management-and-sharing-policies/data-management-and-sharing-policy-overview)**
  (NIH, sharing.nih.gov) — NIH's own plain-language overview. Start here when explaining the policy
  to the CIO. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Writing a Data Management and Sharing Plan](https://sharing.nih.gov/data-management-and-sharing-policy/planning-and-budgeting-for-data-management-and-sharing/writing-a-data-management-and-sharing-plan)**
  (NIH) — what a plan contains. Use it to know what the hub's plan will ask contributors to
  support. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Selecting a Data Repository](https://sharing.nih.gov/data-management-and-sharing-policy/sharing-scientific-data/selecting-a-data-repository)**
  (NIH) — how investigators choose where data goes. Use it to understand the "NIH-designated
  repository" idea behind the clause. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Open Domain-Specific Data Sharing Repositories](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/NIHbmic/domain_specific_repositories.html)**
  (NIH/NLM) — a list of NIH-supported repositories, the one the policy's own footnote points to. Use
  it to see what kinds of repositories exist. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[BioLINCC](https://biolincc.nhlbi.nih.gov/home/)** (NHLBI) — the repository the 2022 paper says
  served the REDS-III public-use data. Use it to see how requesting shared NHLBI data works. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; the page returned an empty `<title>` to `curl`).

- **[45 CFR 164.514, Other requirements relating to uses and disclosures of protected health information](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514)**
  (Cornell LII) — paragraph (e) is the limited data set and DUA text; (a) and (b) are the
  de-identification standard the lesson names but doesn't quote. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR 606.160, Records](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)** (Cornell LII) —
  the BECS record retention rule, paragraph (d), for contrast with the extract. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST IR 8053, De-Identification of Personal Information](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/8053/final)**
  (NIST CSRC) — a technical survey of de-identification techniques and their limits. Useful
  background for the conversation about "further de-identified." It is general, not HIPAA guidance.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIH Video: The NIH Final Policy for Data Management and Sharing is in Effect: Planning for Success!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UbtWG_kjPfw)**
  (NIH Funding, from oEmbed `author_name`; exact oEmbed title as shown) — the video embedded in the
  lesson. A general explainer for funded investigators, not specific to blood centers or contracts.
  Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13; the title also matches NIH's own
  grants.nih.gov video page, which loaded with HTTP 200.

Not listed: HHS's HIPAA de-identification and research pages, which returned 403 (access denied) to
`curl` today. They were not retried. The PubMed Central page for the 2022 paper returned a bot-check
to `curl` earlier (see modules 1 and 2), so module 1's resources page links it instead.

## Keep learning

Not official sources, and not authority for any regulatory claim.

- **[FAIR Principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/)** (GO FAIR Foundation) — the
  community home of the principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) the DMS policy
  says it encourages. Good vocabulary for talking about provenance and metadata. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title "FAIR | GO FAIR Foundation").

- **[The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship](https://www.nature.com/articles/sdata201618)**
  (Wilkinson et al., *Scientific Data*) — the original paper the policy cites. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title matches).

- **[PROV-Overview](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/)** (W3C) — an overview of a standard
  vocabulary for describing where data came from and what happened to it. Heavier than Lakeshore
  needs, but it sharpens what "provenance" can mean. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13
  (HTTP 200; title "PROV-Overview").

- **[UCI GRT Hub: NIH Data Management and Sharing Policy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m1Y_8r3Lv90)**
  (a university research-support group, not NIH) — a second, shorter-form explainer from a research
  institution's perspective. I have not watched it in full. Verified via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13.

- **[FAIR Data and Resources](https://datascience.nih.gov/data-ecosystem)** (NIH Office of Data
  Science Strategy) — NIH's data-ecosystem page, a good launch point for how NIH thinks about
  discoverable, reusable data. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
